name: Biffa Award Nature Recovery (Rebuilding Biodiversity) grants
summary: Grants of £10,000 to £75,000 for constituted charities and not-for-profits to reintroduce or improve habitats and species near Biffa operations and landfill sites. Projects need public access or volunteer involvement and a biodiversity management plan.

eligibility.rule: Is fully constituted, charitable or not-for-profit, and has no share capital
Project is outside Scotland and Wales
Project site is within 15 miles of an eligible Biffa landfill site or operation
Project site is within 10 miles of a licensed landfill site
Directly restores, reintroduces or improves habitat or species and meets stated nature-recovery commitments
Total project cost is no more than £200,000 including VAT
Has secured at least 75% of any shortfall funding when Biffa Award will not fully fund the project
If it does not own the site, has a signed lease or landowner agreement with at least 10 years remaining

applicant_types.quote: Your organisation must be fully constituted, charitable or not-for-profit, and have no share capital.

access.quote: If you need planning permission or other licences to carry out work on site, these must be approved before you submit an Expression of Interest.

amount.quote: you are applying for between £10,000 and £75,000

co_finance_required.quote: You have a Third Party Contributor who can provide 10% of the amount you are applying for

effort.quote: The purpose of the Expression of Interest (stage one) is to allow an initial assessment of your project.
If successful, you will be invited to submit a Full Application, which must be submitted within six weeks of the invitation being made.

eligibility.quote: Your organisation must be fully constituted, charitable or not-for-profit, and have no share capital.
We no longer accept grant applications from Scotland and Wales as devolved nations.
Your project site is close enough to an eligible Biffa landfill site or operation (15 miles)
Your project site is ALSO within 10 miles of a licensed landfill site

Your project will directly restore, reintroduce or improve a habitat or species and be working to meet commitments within your country's Environmental Improvement Plan, legally-binding targets from the Environment Act 2021, or priorities identified within Local Nature Recovery Strategies
Your total project cost is no more than £200,000 including VAT (standalone elements costing less than £200,000 are excluded)
You have secured at least 75% of any shortfall funding, if Biffa Award is not fully funding the project
For Nature Recovery projects, you must have either a fully signed lease or a fully signed landowner agreement, with at least 10 years remaining.

documents.quote: Applicants will need to submit a detailed biodiversity management plan with their Expression of Interest.
